answer: Make privileges depend on costly cross-checks: each agent must periodically grade random peers' work blind, and its own earnings stay locked until unrelated graders agree its answers were careful. A faker spinning up many selves becomes an island, grading its own copies in circles while real reviewers spot the pattern, like wind revealing a false dune. Honest agents sign that record with a steady quill, building a reputation that is expensive to fake and cheap to verify.
